name: Kalibook
author: mundfdevelopment

sections.description:
Kalibook lets a small service business – a hair salon, a practice, a consultant, a workshop – take appointments online and manage them in the WordPress admin. You define your services and weekly opening hours; visitors pick a service, a day and a free time in a booking form on your site; you see everything in a week calendar.

It is built for the one-person business that currently juggles a paper diary or a spreadsheet: no external service, no account anywhere, no monthly fee. Everything lives in your own WordPress database.

Features:

  • Services with duration, buffer time after the appointment, price and calendar colour
  • Weekly opening hours with up to four intervals per day (lunch breaks) and time off (holidays, sick days)
  • Slot engine: free start times on a configurable grid, with minimum notice and a booking horizon
  • Appointments with automatic numbers (KB-YYYY-NNNNN) and a status workflow: pending, confirmed, completed, no-show, cancelled
  • No double bookings: every save re-checks overlaps (including buffer time and time off) under a database lock
  • Week calendar with a time grid, single-day view on phones, and a dashboard with today and the next seven days
  • Customer management with appointment history
  • The “Kalibook Booking Form” block: service → day → time → contact details → confirmation
  • Online bookings as requests to confirm, or confirmed automatically
  • Spam protection with honeypot, time token and rate limit instead of a captcha
  • E-mails on new requests, confirmation and cancellation, plus a reminder the day before, with editable templates
  • Setup assistant: company, opening hours and first service in about three minutes
  • Translation-ready; German is provided through translate.wordpress.org

Time zones, done properly

All appointments are stored as UTC instants and shown in your site’s time zone. Days with a daylight-saving change are handled: a wall time that does not exist is never offered, and a 23- or 25-hour day keeps its correct slots.

Privacy

Kalibook sends nothing anywhere. There are no external fonts, no CDN and no tracking in the admin or on the frontend, and customer data stays in your WordPress database. The booking form stores no IP addresses — the spam protection works on hashes and a hidden field. Visitors never see other customers’ appointments, only free times.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/kalibook, or install it through Plugins > Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” menu in WordPress.
  3. Open “Kalibook” in the admin menu; the setup assistant asks for your company details, opening hours and first service.
  4. Under Kalibook > Settings, check the booking rules (start-time grid, minimum notice, booking horizon, automatic confirmation) and the e-mail sender address.
  5. Put the “Kalibook Booking Form” block on a page and publish it.

Requirements: WordPress 6.4 or newer and PHP 8.2 or newer. Kalibook creates its own database tables on activation; it does not store appointments as posts or custom post types.
sections.faq:
Does uninstalling delete my data?

No. Data is only removed when “Delete all data on uninstall” is enabled in Kalibook > Settings. Deactivating the plugin never deletes anything.

Can two customers book the same time?

No. Before an appointment is saved, Kalibook checks it against all pending and confirmed appointments (including their buffer time) and your time off, inside a database lock. If someone else was faster, the visitor is asked to choose another time.

Can I book outside my opening hours?

In the admin, yes: choose “Custom time” in the appointment form. Overlaps are still refused. The public booking form only offers times inside the opening hours.

Do online bookings need my confirmation?

By default they arrive as “pending” and already block the time until you confirm or cancel them. Turn on “Confirm online bookings automatically” under Settings > Booking rules to skip that step. There is no online payment in the free version.

How is the booking form protected against spam?

With a hidden honeypot field, a signed time token (a form submitted in under three seconds is rejected) and a per-hour rate limit. Optionally the e-mail domain can be checked for a DNS record. No captcha, no third-party service, and no IP address is stored.

Which e-mails does Kalibook send, and can I change the wording?

Request received (to the customer and to you), appointment confirmed, appointment cancelled, and a reminder the day before. Subject and body of every template are editable under Kalibook > Settings > E-mail, with placeholders such as {{customer_name}} and {{appointment_number}}. Clearing a template resets it to the default.

Does Kalibook work with my theme?

The admin is a React application inside wp-admin and does not touch your theme. The booking form block renders its own markup with kb- prefixed classes and loads no external assets, so it inherits your theme’s typography and colours.

Is there a German version?

The interface is fully translatable through the text domain kalibook. Translations, including German, are provided through translate.wordpress.org.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Services, weekly opening hours and time off.
  • Slot engine with start-time grid, buffer, minimum notice and booking horizon.
  • Appointments with numbers, status workflow and conflict check under a database lock.
  • Week calendar, dashboard and customer appointment history.
  • Dashboard: number of no-shows this month and the estimated lost revenue.
  • Booking form block with a public API, honeypot, time token and rate limit.
  • Transactional e-mails with editable templates and a daily reminder.
  • Setting “Business phone” (Settings > General) and the e-mail placeholder {{company_phone}}.
  • Developer hooks for slots, appointments, REST responses, e-mails and the booking form, plus appointment meta storage.
